theMappingStatement.verdict: There is NO arithmetic mapping between the two counters, and none is defined here. The bridge is a REFETCH -- the smaller answer task 6.4's own NON-CLAIMS name as admissible ('a refetch of the source record is an admissible answer and may be the smaller one', tasks.md:103).
theMappingStatement.counterA: The `SerializedCampaign` row `version`. It is the whole-envelope PUT's compare-and-swap token (`CampaignPersistenceService.ts:103-158`; client side `useCampaignPersistenceStore.baseVersion`), and it is what the source-side acceptance write advances to `sourceRowVersion + 1` (pinned on main by the 6.2a-3 review, `versionAdvancedConsistently`: 'Both the COLUMN and the envelope's own `version` move to `sourceRowVersion + 1` ... a client that refetches after an acceptance gets a `baseVersion` the next PUT will win with').
theMappingStatement.counterB: The journal stream revision the command route compares (`expectedRevision` in `campaignCommandPipeline.ts`; `ICampaignEvent.sequence`, and 6.2b's original receipt revision plus current public head). Command-route-only. It counts appended events on a stream; the row version counts clean writes to a table row. Neither is computable from the other.
theMappingStatement.whichRevisionTheCacheKeyIs: Task 1.3's `(instanceId, revision)` cache key is keyed by the `SerializedCampaign` row `version` -- the PUT CAS token -- NOT by any journal revision. This is stated in code (`useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts`, the `refreshAfterCommittedCommand` doc block and the `ICampaignCommittedCommandAck` doc block) and here.
theMappingStatement.whyThisContradictsNothing: It is what the code already does rather than a new decision: `campaignCacheKeyOf` (`src/lib/campaign/persistence/campaignCacheKey.ts`) builds the key as `{ instanceId: record.instanceId ?? null, revision: record.version }` -- `revision` is read straight off the `SerializedCampaign` row version. Task 1.3's own receipt calls the pair 'the hosting instance that wrote it and the revision it was taken from', with no claim that the revision is a stream revision. The task-6.4 STOP condition ('if the code cannot state that without contradicting task 1.3's text, STOP') was evaluated against `campaignCacheKey.ts` and 1.3's receipt text and did NOT fire.

theMappingStatement.postAcknowledgementRefresh: When the command route acknowledges a committed command (`kind: 'committed'`), the client calls `refreshAfterCommittedCommand(ack)`: it ignores an acknowledgement whose `state.campaignId` is not the loaded campaign, clears the armed auto-save (which still holds the pre-command token), and re-reads the record through the ONE existing load path (`runLoad` -> `fetchCampaignRecord`), publishing the read as `inFlightLoad` so a concurrent write waits for it. `runLoad` then does what it already does: the task-1.3 cache verdict (revision-diverged -> replace whole), the roster-projection restore, the cache-key stamp, and `baseVersion` = the refetched row `version`.

sourceReplayFenceCoordination.why: Clause (a) of task 6.4 names a `sourceReplayFence` refusal explicitly. That fence is task 6.1's, implemented on the local branch `codex/roadmap-r2-61-source-replay-fence-20260915` at `ac2782f4e` (receipt `evidence/r2-61-source-replay-fence-local-20260915.json`) and NOT on origin/main at this base. Its guard refuses any whole-envelope PUT whose envelope does not echo the stored fence, judged AHEAD of the `baseVersion` CAS -- so a client that refreshed but dropped the fence would still be refused, and clause (a) would be unmet.
sourceReplayFenceCoordination.whatThisSliceAdded: The optional field `SerializedCampaign.sourceReplayFence?: ICampaignSourceReplayFence` plus the `ICampaignSourceReplayFence` interface, copied VERBATIM from `ac2782f4e:src/types/campaign/SerializedCampaign.ts` (byte-identical text and identical insertion point, verified by diff this session), and the client half: the store holds the fence from every record it reads (`applySavedRecord`, `runLoad`, `rollbackCoopCampaign`, `resolveConflictTakeServer`) and echoes it on the ordinary save (`putLiveCampaign`) and on the discard-time keepalive flush.
sourceReplayFenceCoordination.clientNeverMintsIt: `withSourceReplayFence` attaches the held value or nothing at all (conditional spread, never an enumerable `undefined`), so an unfenced campaign sends exactly the envelope it sent before the field existed. The server strips and re-stamps it (`withoutClientFence` on the 6.1 branch); the client only ever proves it has SEEN a materialization.
sourceReplayFenceCoordination.flushDigestUnaffected: `flushedEnvelopeDigest` hashes schemaVersion / campaignId / savedAt / originDeviceId / body only, so adding the fence to an outgoing envelope does not change the digest the post-flush reconciliation compares. Verified by the crash-window suite staying green (23 rows).

nonClaims: NO 6.2b CALLER. Nothing in production calls `refreshAfterCommittedCommand`. The client routing that submits the acceptance command is task 6.2b, which is owner-blocked on the identity/seat decision and is not on main; the caller lands with 6.2b. The bridge ships with its behaviour proven so 6.2b has something to call rather than inventing one.

NO WIDENING OF THE `/commands` RESPONSE. The route is untouched. `ICampaignCommittedCommandAck` declares `receiptRevision` and `publicHead` as OPTIONAL precisely because they are 6.2b's to add; the bridge reads neither as a row version and works without them.
NO FLAG FLIP, NO CUTOVER, NO CAMP WITNESS.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE SOURCE WRITES THE ROW TODAY ON THIS BASE: that is 6.2a-3, already on main (#1706-#1708), and the fence that makes an un-echoed PUT fail is 6.1, NOT on main. Until 6.1 lands the fence field is inert in production -- absent on every row, so `fenceOf` yields null and every envelope is byte-identical to today's.

THE DIRTY-CLIENT CASE IS NOT SOLVED, IT IS INHERITED. If a client has unsaved local mutations when the acknowledgement arrives, `runLoad`'s task-1.3 verdict replaces the cached copy WHOLE and those mutations are lost -- which is the existing replace-not-merge law, not a new behaviour, and is why 6.2a's client half obtains an acknowledged save BEFORE submitting the command. It is not pinned by a row here and is recorded as a residual for 6.2b / cutover rather than claimed closed.

THE 409 RETRY-NOISE RESIDUAL IS NOT RETIRED. This slice does not change `commands.ts:208-217`, whose `offer-not-durable` advice ('an acknowledged save fixes it') the 6.2a-3 re-review found inaccurate for an already-committed same-actor retry. Correcting that advice needs the client routing that reads it, i.e. 6.2b.
`CampaignGmArbiter` remains a second AcceptContract writer that does not reduce the row (carried forward from the 6.2a-3 receipts, untouched here).

RE_A1.finding: `refreshAfterCommittedCommandAction` called `clearAutoSaveTimer()` and never re-armed, so on every non-adopting `runLoad` path a dirty client was left with NO pending write -- the failure the crash-window F1 fix in the same file exists to close, which `reconcileAfterDiscardFlushAction` closes by arming on every path.
RE_A1.fix: `runLoad(set, campaignId).then((adopted) => { if (!adopted && get().dirty) { armAutoSaveTimer(set, get); } return adopted; })`. Guarded rather than unconditional because the ADOPTING path clears `dirty`, so arming there would fire a write with nothing to say -- the sibling's unconditional arm is right for the sibling, whose adopt path deliberately sets `dirty: true`.
RE_A1.newRow: 'leaves a dirty client with a pending write when the refetch does not answer' -- dirty client, GET 500, NO intervening `markDirty()`, advance `AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS`, assert one PUT at the pre-command token and `dirty` still true.
RE_A1.redThenGreen: RED against the committed product code (d036f3611's store restored over the new test file): 1 failed / 5 passed, the failing row being exactly this one. GREEN with the fix: 6 passed / 6.
RE_A1.whyTheOldRowMissedIt: Confirmed as the reviewer stated: the pre-existing refetch-failure row calls `markDirty()` AFTER the failed refresh, and `markDirtyAction` arms the timer itself, so the missing re-arm was masked.

RE_A2.finding: The doc block's list of what the action does not do read as exhaustive and omitted that this is the one refetch-replace call site without task 1.3's dirty-state exemption.
RE_A2.fix: A paragraph added to the action's doc block stating plainly: this call site has no `!dirty` exemption (the page shell's does, and defers dirty state to the save path's conflict handling, which this function has just cancelled); an acknowledgement arriving while the client is dirty DISCARDS those unsaved local mutations; that is a loss of local work and never a silent overwrite of the server; it is tolerable only because 6.2a's client half obtains an acknowledged save before submitting; and the `!dirty` guard is deliberately NOT added because trading the lost edit for an unexplained 409 is 6.2b's design call.
RE_A2.nonDemandHonored: The reviewer's explicit non-demand was honored -- no `!dirty` guard was added.

fenceOnConflictCheck.question: The 6.1 review's non-blocking note says `resolveConflictTakeServerAction` adopts through `metadataFrom`, which drops `sourceReplayFence`, leaving the campaign unsaveable after a fence 409; the 6.4 review says the 409's `current` carries the fence and take-server adopts it. Which is true?
fenceOnConflictCheck.verdict: THE 6.4 REVIEW IS RIGHT FOR THIS STACK, and the 6.1 note is right about `metadataFrom` alone. Read in code at d036f3611: `metadataFrom` projects six fields and does NOT carry the fence -- but this slice does not carry the fence in `metadata`. It is its own store field, and `resolveConflictTakeServerAction`'s `set({...})` includes `sourceReplayFence: fenceOf(migrated)` alongside `metadata: metadataFrom(migrated)`. So nothing was dropped and NO threading fix was required.
supportingReads: `readConflictBody` returns `typed.current` as the record whenever the typed 409 shape is present, so the whole stored envelope -- fence included -- reaches `conflictServerRecord`.

`migrateClientRecord` -> `migrateSerializedCampaign`: every ladder step spreads `...snapshot` (`campaignMigration.ts:59`, `:82`, `:85`), so an unknown-to-the-ladder field like `sourceReplayFence` survives migration untouched.
rowsAddedAnyway: 'does not retry a fence refusal that names the very token the client sent' -- pins fact (a): a PURE fence refusal returns `currentVersion` EQUAL to the client's `baseVersion` (the row never moved; only the watermark was missing), and the client answers it with exactly ONE PUT and a `conflict` state. No 'versions match, so retry' heuristic exists, and this row would fail if one were added.

'restores a saveable client when the server record is taken after a fence refusal' -- pins that take-server adopts the fence from the 409's `current`, so the next ordinary save carries it and is acknowledged 200.
fenceOnConflictCheck.honestStatusOfThoseTwoRows: GREEN ON ARRIVAL, not red-first, because the behaviour they pin was already correct in d036f3611. Stated rather than dressed up as a fix. They are falsified 1:1 instead: deleting `sourceReplayFence: fenceOf(migrated)` from the take-server `set` turns the second row red and leaves the other five green (measured this session).
fenceOnConflictCheck.factB_digest: CONFIRMED BY READING, and deliberately NOT given a test row. `flushedEnvelopeDigest` hashes `schemaVersion`, `campaignId`, `savedAt`, `originDeviceId` and `body` only -- the fence is absent, so echoing one cannot disturb the post-flush reconciliation's comparison. A behavioural row would be VACUOUS here: the client echoes exactly the fence it read and the server re-stamps that same value, so both sides of the digest comparison would carry it and the row would stay green even if the fence WERE included. A code fact with no falsifiable behaviour is confirmed, not simulated.
fenceOnConflictCheck.finalPlacement: Both fence-conflict rows live in commit B, not A. They pin behaviour commit A already had right, so they are pins rather than proofs, and B is the pin commit. Their falsification is unchanged and still 1:1: deleting `sourceReplayFence: fenceOf(migrated)` from the take-server `set` turns the take-server row red and leaves every other row green.
